body: Large language models are increasingly used as judges to reduce reliance on costly human evaluation, yet their scores can systematically disagree with human judgments. We ask whether responses to an explicitly imposed evaluative bias can help correct a judge's implicit scoring biases. We introduce PRISM (Probe-based Residual Inference of Scoring Misalignment), which holds the evaluated content fixed and measures score changes when attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized. A local sensitivity model motivates representing these responses as a surrogate Jacobian. Ridge regression on human labels learns a correction to the baseline score. The resulting scoring protocol is rubric-free: it uses overall scores without requesting criterion-level ratings. In the main Jev and Sol comparisons on SummEval summarization and HANNA story evaluation, PRISM and its learned-baseline variant significantly improve agreement with human rankings over uncalibrated scores while remaining competitive with rubric-based methods. A controlled SummEval comparison yields similar agreement for rubric-derived quality probes and style probes, supporting calibration without reproducing rubric criteria. The learned coefficients reveal shared and opposing correction directions across judges.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了PRISM（基于探针的评分失调残差推理）方法，旨在校准大模型作为裁判时的系统性偏差。通过固定评估内容并测量属性强调下的分数变化，该方法利用代理雅可比矩阵和岭回归学习偏差修正，无需预设评分准则。实验表明，PRISM在SummEval和HANNA数据集上显著提升了与人类评价的一致性，为大模型评估提供了更高效、鲁棒的校准方案。
